name: Adamastor
body:
Adamastor CR 19

This enormous humanoid is massively muscled, though its flesh shows what should be fatal wounds. Its sunken eyes and sagging features contort in anger and pain.

XP 204,800
NE Colossal undead (evil, extraplanar, titan)
Init +0; Senses darkvision 120 ft., mistsight, true seeing; Perception +32

DEFENSE

AC 34, touch 2, flat-footed 34 (+32 natural, –8 size)
hp 351 (26d8+234)
Fort +19, Ref +8, Will +20
Defensive Abilities rock catching; DR 20/epic and good; Immune electricity, undead traits

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., swim 40 ft.; air walk
Melee +2 ghost touch shocking burst greataxe +30/+25/+20/+15 (6d8+27/19–20/x3) or bite +29 (8d8+25 plus grab)
Ranged rock +12/+7/+2 (8d6+25)
Space 30 ft.; Reach 30 ft.
Special Attacks roar, swallow whole (6d8+25 bludgeoning damage plus 2d8 acid damage, AC 26, 35 hp)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 20th; concentration +29)

Constant—air walk, true seeing, freedom of movement
At will—call lightning storm (DC 24), commune with nature, divination, fog cloud, hydraulic torrent

STATISTICS

Str 45, Dex 10, Con —, Int 12, Wis 17, Cha 29
Base Atk +19; CMB +44 (+48 bull rush or grapple); CMD 54 (56 vs. bull rush)
Feats Cleave, Critical Focus, Great Cleave, Great Fortitude, Greater Bull Rush, Greater Vital Strike, Improved Bull Rush, Improved Critical (greataxe), Improved Vital Strike, Iron Will, Power Attack, Vital Strike, Weapon Focus (bite)
Skills Acrobatics +26 (+30 to jump), Climb +34, Intimidate +38, Knowledge (nature) +15, Perception +32, Profession (sailor) +15, Swim +45
Languages Abyssal, Common; telepathy 100 ft.
Gear +2 ghost touch shocking burst greataxe

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Fogbank (Sp)

When an adamastor uses its fog cloud spell-like ability, the radius of the fog is increased to 50 feet. In addition, it can continue concentrating on creating the fog each round, increasing its radius by an additional 50 feet, up to a maximum 500-foot radius if it concentrates for 1 minute. The fog cloud it creates cannot be dissipated by wind unless the wind affects the entire area of fog. This fogbank cannot extend more than 20 feet onto land, unless the entire area of the land fits within its area, such as small rocks, reefs, and islets.

Living Spirit (Su)

An adamastor’s physical remains typically lie petrified at the bottom of the ocean. At any time, it can manifest its spirit anywhere within 100 miles of its remains as a translucent image of its true form. This functions as project image but does not require line of effect; however, this image must remain within, on, or adjacent to the sea and no more than 60 feet above its surface. Creating this living spirit is a standard action, but it can be dismissed as a free action.

Once per day, it can incarnate itself into its physical form at the location of this projected image, forming a physical body with all of its powers and abilities. It can maintain this form for up to 1 hour. In this form, it can move up away from the sea, but each round it spends farther away than the limits described above counts as 1 minute toward the time it can maintain its body. In addition, as a swift action, an adamastor can become incorporeal (or return from being incorporeal to being material); however, each round it spends incorporeal also counts as 1 minute toward the time it can maintain its incarnated body.

When this time limit ends or when the adamastor’s body is reduced to 0 hit points, its body and its gear collapse in a cascade of frothing salt water and it cannot reform a physical body again for 2d4 days. The only way to permanently destroy the adamastor is to locate its remains and free it from its divine curse, the method of which should be determined by the GM.

Mistsight (Ex)

An adamastor can see through fog, mist, and murky water as if they were perfectly clear, ignoring the miss chance for such obscurement, up to its normal range of vision.

Roar (Su)

As a full-round action, an adamastor lets out a terrifying roar forcing all creatures in a 60-foot-radius burst to succeed on a DC 32 Will save or become frightened for 2d6 rounds. This is a mind-affecting, fear effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Shipwrecker (Ex)

An adamastor’s axe deals double damage to objects made of wood.

ECOLOGY

Environment any ocean
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Adamastors are undead titans, towering humanoids of immense size. Slain in ancient wars with the gods, their deathless spirit endures in the depths of the sea. They generally inhabit rocky straits and continental capes, avenging their fury upon sailors of the sea and smashing their vessels when they dare to explore beyond the bounds of familiar waters.

An adamastor’s flesh is translucent and its underlying features are heroic but faded and worn, with heavy jowls, a long scraggly beard, hollow eyes, and an earthy pale complexion. His wild hair is matted with clay, and his mouth is full of teeth that have long since turned to black and yellow from decay. Adamastors are 60 feet tall and weigh 15 tons.

Adamastors are often seen as a personification of the sea’s perilous nature. They are sometimes seen in a tragic light, the dying embers of a divine ambition, now lonely and melancholic under their divine curse. Some even revere them as embodying the challenges and bravery inherent to nautical exploration, a symbol of maritime history and exploration and the open horizon of possibility, while others see them as a symbol of arrogance, a conquest, and imperialism. However they are viewed by sailors, adamastors can sometimes be founts of knowledge about the oceans if caught in a sanguine mood, but approaching their haunts is dangerous indeed and rarely worth risking ship and crew.

The elder titans strove with the nascent gods and godlings in the earliest ages but their rebellion against divine authority was quelled. Some became servants of the gods and others were cursed with eternal torment or eternal imprisonment.

Others were slain in the divine war and cast into the sea, but their spark of immortality left them unable to ever truly die and they became titans of the deep. The abysmal depths quenched the seething wrath of some, as they calcified into mountainous living reefs, and some even repented of their legacy of cruelty and death, but for most their loathing of the gods and their children endured throughout the ages has driven them to rise from their pelagic torpor to ravage the shipping lanes until their thirst for destruction is slaked and then fall back into the lightless depths for another generation until the furnace of their hate once more awakens them to wrath and ruin.
